function: Estimating the multi-user XL-MIMO channel from uplink pilots for near-field and far-field users, by refining LS estimates with a CNN (XLCNet), plus a compressed version (pp. 1-3).
system: TDD multi-user XL-MIMO, ULA BS with 256 antennas at half-wavelength spacing, K users (H is M x K), wavelength 0.01 m (30 GHz band cited), no RIS (pp. 1-4).
method: CNN denoiser XLCNet (nine 2D convolutional layers, residual), supervised with MSE loss on LS estimates; compressed by magnitude pruning with fine-tuning and post-training weight quantization (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: Synthetic hybrid-field channels (eq. 9, from [8]), M=256: 90,000 training and 10,000 validation samples with L=6, L0=1; 2,000 test samples of pure near-field or far-field channels (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained once on hybrid-field data (L=6, L0=1); tested on near-field-only and far-field-only channels with L=3 and L=6, versus match-trained models, SNR -10 to 20 dB (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE, HOMP [8]. Learned: V-MRDN, a variant of the multiple residual dense network of [15] (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR and versus quantization bit-width; number of weights and run time; model-size and complexity reduction factors (pp. 4-5).
complexity: FLOPs order O(M Nw) for XLCNet and O(M(1-kappa)Nw) for C-XLCNet; 263K weights and 0.2 ms versus 29K weights and 0.078 ms at kappa=0.9, b=8 (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "XLCNet is trained based on the data generated by the hybrid-field channel model [8]", a custom model with i.i.d. complex Gaussian path gains and ULA steering vectors (Eqs. 3-5); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "the testing set, generated based on the near-field or far-field channel model, contains 2,000 samples" while training uses the hybrid-field model with L = 6; p. 5: "Although XLCNet is trained with L = 6 and L0 = 1, it achieves the almost same accuracy as the match training case".
q3_support: p. 4: "include the LS estimator, linear minimum MSE (LMMSE) estimator, hybrid-field orthogonal matching pursuit (HOMP) [8], and a variant version of multiple residual dense network [15], named V-MRDN", all compared on NMSE in Figs. 3-5 (pp. 4-5).
q4_support: p. 4: "The complexity of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is selected as the metric." with O(M Nw) in Eqs. 17-19, and weights and run time in Table I (p. 5).
q5_support: p. 4: "generated based on the hybrid-field channel model in (9)"; the data are simulated by the authors and the paper gives no link or DOI for code or data and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 2: channel estimation, XLCNet refines LS estimates (p. 2). No RIS in the system; RIS appears only in references [13] and [15] (p. 5). q2 is counted for the test on pure near-field or far-field channels and on L=3 after training on hybrid-field data with L=6 (pp. 4-5), not for the SNR sweep. q3: V-MRDN is a published CNN estimator [15] adapted by the authors, so it is an earlier learned method and not a variant of XLCNet.
